readings.c1s1:
name for a receptacle of inflorescence, such as that of ''Compositæ''.

'''Anthocorinæ''' (an-thok-ō-rī′nē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Anthocoris'' + ''-inæ''.] A subfamily of bugs, of the family ''Cimicidæ'', containing chiefly minute, narrowly oval, and narrow-headed species of a shining-black or dull-brown color, marked with white.

'''Anthocoris''' (an-thok′ọ-ris), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + κόρις, a bug.] A genus of heteropterous insects, of the family ''Lygæidæ'', or giving name to a subfamily ''Anthocorinæ'' of the family ''Cimicidæ'', having the antennæ filiform. It contains small black bugs with reddish and white marks. See cut under ''flower-bug''.

'''anthocyan''' (an-thọ̄-sī′a̤n), ''n.'' Same as ''anthocyanin''.

'''anthocyanin, anthocyanine''' (an-thọ̄-sī′a̤-nin), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + κύανος, blue, + ''-in''<sup>2</sup>. Cf. ''cyanin''.] The dissolved coloring matter in blue flowers.

'''anthodium''' (an-thō′di-um), ''n.''; pl. ''anthodia'' (-ä̤). [NL., < Gr. ἀνθώδης: see ''anthoid''.] The head, or so-called compound flower, of ''Compositæ''.

'''anthogenesis''' (an-thọ̄-jen′e-sis), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + γένεσις, production.] A mode of reproduction occurring in some of the plant-lice, or ''Phytophthiria'', in which there intervenes a form furnishing male and female pupæ from which sexual individuals arise. ''Pascoe'', Zoöl.
readings.c1s2:
Class., p. 264.

'''anthography''' (an-thog′ra-fi), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + -γραφία, < γράφειν, write.] That branch of botany which treats of flowers; a description of flowers.

'''anthoid''' (an′thoid), ''a.'' [< Gr. *ἀνθοειδής, contr. ἀνθώδης, like a flower, < ἄνθος, a flower, + εἶδος, form.] Having the form of a flower; resembling a flower.

'''antholeucin, antholeucine''' (an-thọ̄-lū′sin), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + λευκός, white, + ''-in''<sup>2</sup>.] The dissolved coloring matter in white flowers.

'''antholite''' (an′thọ̄-līt), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + λίθος, a stone.] In ''geol.'', an impression on rocks, as on the shales of the coal-measures, resembling, or supposed to resemble, a flower.

'''anthological'''<sup>1</sup> (an-thọ̄-loj′i-kal), ''a.'' [< ''anthology''<sup>1</sup>.] Pertaining to an anthology; consisting of beautiful extracts, especially from the poets.

'''anthological'''<sup>2</sup>† (an-thọ̄-loj′i-ka̤l), ''a.'' [< ''anthology''<sup>2</sup>.] Treating of flowers.

'''anthologist''' (an-thol′ọ̄-jist), ''n.'' [< ''anthology''<sup>1</sup> + ''-ist.''] The compiler of an anthology.

'''anthology'''<sup>1</sup> (an-thol′ọ̄-ji), ''n.''; pl. ''anthologies'' (-jiz). [< Gr. ἀνθολογία, LGr. also ἀνθολόγιον, a flower-gathering, and hence a collection of small poems, < ἀνθολόγος, gathering flowers, < ἄνθος, a flower, + λέγειν = L. ''legere'', gather, read: see ''lection'', ''legend'', etc., and cf. ''anthology''<sup>2</sup>.] '''1.''' A collection of flowers; a garland. [Rare.]—
readings.c1s3:
¶

'''2.''' A collection of poems, epigrams, and fugitive pieces by various authors. {{smaller|The name was originally given to Greek collections of this nature, and is hence applied to any literary collection similarly made.}}

'''3.''' In the ''Gr. Ch.'', a selection from several of the official service-books of such parts of the services as are most needed by the laity.

'''anthology'''<sup>2</sup>'''†''' (an-thol′ọ-ji), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + -λογία, < λέγειν, speak: see ''-ology''.] A treatise on flowers.

'''antholysis''' (an-thol′i-sis), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + λύσις, a breaking up, a loosening, < λύειν, loosen.] In ''bot.'', a retrograde metamorphosis of the organs of a flower, as of carpels into stamens, stamens into petals, etc.

'''anthomania''' (an-thō-mā′ni-ä̤), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + μανία, mania: see ''mania''.] An extravagant fondness for flowers.

'''Anthomedusa''' (an″thō-mē-dū′sä̤), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + NL. ''medusa'', q. v.] The typical genus of the family ''Anthomedusidæ''.

'''anthomedusid''' (an″thō-mē-dū′sid), ''n.'' An acaleph of the family ''Anthomedusidæ''.

'''Anthomedusidæ''' (an″thō-mē-dū′si-dē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Anthomedusa'' + ''-idæ''.] In ''zoöl.'', a family of ''Hydromedusinæ'' (which see) whose medusæ become free. {{smaller|They are without otoliths, with ocelli at the base of the tentacles, gonads on the outer wall of the gastral cavity, and mostly 4 radial canals. The polyp-colonies on which these medusæ bud contain alimentary zoöids which are not invested by chitinous cups. The medusæ bud mostly on the ordinary alimentary polyps, but exceptionally directly from the hydrorhiza.}}

'''anthophyllitic''' (an″thō-fi-lit′ik), ''a.'' [< ''anthophyllite'' + ''-ic''.] Pertaining to anthophyllite, or containing it.

'''Anthophysa''' (an-thọ̄-fī′zä̤), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + φῦσα, a breath, bubble.] A genus of pantostomatous infusorians, of the group ''Dimastiga'', containing biflagellate monads which are united in colonies of several zoöids.

'''Anthoptilidæ''' (an-thop-til′i-dē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Anthoptilon'' + ''-idæ''.] A family of spicateous pennatuloid polyps without rachial pinnules, with polyps sessile on both sides of the rachis in distinct rows, and without cells.

'''Anthoptilon''' (an-thop′ti-lon), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, flower, + πτίλον, feather, wing.] A genus of polyps, representing the family ''Anthoptilidæ''.

'''anthorism''' (an′thō-rizm), ''n.'' [< NL. ''anthorismus'', < Gr. ἀνθορισμός, counter-definition, < ἀνθορίζειν, make a counter-definition, < ἀνθ-, ἀντ- for ἀντί, against, counter to, + ὁρίζειν, limit, bound, define: see ''horizon''.] In ''rhet.'', a description or definition contrary to that which has been given by one’s opponent.

'''anthorismus''' (an-thọ̄-riz′mus), ''n.'' Same as ''anthorism''.

'''anthosiderite''' (an-thọ̄-sid′e̤-rīt), ''n.'' [< Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + σιδηρίτης, of iron: see ''siderite''.] A native silicate of iron, of an ocherous-yellow color, inclining to yellowish-brown, and having a fibrous radiated structure, found in Brazil.

'''Anthosoma''' (an-thō-sō′mä), ''n.'' [NL., < Gr. ἄνθος, a flower, + σῶμα, a body.] A genus of siphonostomous parasitic crustaceans, giving name to a family ''Anthosomidæ''. A species, ''A. smithi'', is found upon sharks.

'''Anthosomidæ''' (an-thō-sō′mi-dē), ''n. pl.'' [NL., < ''Anthosoma'' + ''-idæ''.] A family of siphonostomous parasitic crustaceans, typified by the genus ''Anthosoma''.

'''Anthomyzidæ''' (an-thō-mī′zi-dē), ''n. pl.''   [NL., < ''Anthomyza'', 1, + ''-idæ.'']   Same as ''Anthomyidæ''. '''Anthomyzides''' (an-thō-mī′zi-dēz), ''n. pl.''   [NL., prop.
